stem:
Fig. 2.1 is a transmission electron micrograph showing a section of a specialised epithelial cell found in the lining of the stomach. This cell produces extracellular proteins that are released into the bloodstream.
{{figure:figure_2_1.webp}}
$\times 6000$
Fig. 2.1

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the role of structure **X** and structure **Y**, as shown in Fig. 2.1, in the production of extracellular proteins.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem:
The cell in Fig. 2.1 releases ghrelin, a small protein that acts as a cell signalling molecule.
Fig. 2.2 shows the sequence of amino acids in a ghrelin molecule.
The amino acid serine (Ser) in position 3 in Fig. 2.2 has been modified by the addition of a saturated fatty acid chain.
{{figure:figure_2_2.webp}}
Fig. 2.2

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: State the level of protein structure shown in Fig. 2.2.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State **one** similarity between the structure of a saturated fatty acid molecule and an amino acid molecule.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text:
The addition of the fatty acid chain allows ghrelin to function as a cell signalling molecule.
Suggest how the addition of this fatty acid chain allows a ghrelin molecule to act as a cell signalling molecule.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Scientists have discovered that the gene coding for ghrelin contains 5000 base pairs. This is a much larger number of base pairs than is needed to code for the ghrelin molecule shown in Fig. 2.2.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Calculate the percentage of base pairs found in the gene that codes for the ghrelin molecule shown in Fig. 2.2.
Show your working and give your answer to one decimal place.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The primary transcript produced from the ghrelin gene is a longer molecule than the mRNA found in the cytoplasm.
Explain how the primary transcript is modified before translation.
